trial_title: Temozolomide in Treating Patients With Recurrent or Progressive Malignant Glioma
brief_summary:
RATIONALE: Drugs used in chemotherapy use different ways to stop tumor cells from dividing so they stop growing or die.

PURPOSE: Phase II trial to study the effectiveness of temozolomide in treating patients who have recurrent or progressive malignant glioma.

eligibility_table.criterion: Histologically proven recurrent or progressive malignant glioma of one of the following types: Anaplastic oligodendroglioma or oligoastrocytoma, Anaplastic astrocytoma, Glioblastoma multiforme (stratum closed to accrual 11/30/01)
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has anaplastic astrocytoma, which qualifies as a recurrent or progressive malignant glioma.

eligibility_table.criterion: Patients who have failed radiotherapy are eligible
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has undergone prior radiation therapy and is currently experiencing disease progression.

eligibility_table.justification: There is no information provided about measurable disease via CT scan or MRI.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient undergone a CT scan or MRI within the last 30 days that shows measurable disease defined as a tumor size of ≥1 cm in any dimension?

eligibility_table.criterion: At least 6 weeks since other prior chemotherapy

eligibility_table.criterion: At least 3 months since prior radiotherapy (exceptions allowed for recurrent/progressive disease at discretion of primary investigator)
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has undergone prior radiation therapy, and given the timeline of treatments, it is likely that at least 3 months have passed since the last radiotherapy.
The patient has a history of severe lower extremity weakness and urinary retention, indicating that they may not have fully recovered from prior surgeries related to their condition.
The patient is currently on multiple medications including high-dose steroids, temozolomide, CPT-11, and Avastin, which may be considered investigational agents depending on the trial's criteria.
There is no indication in the patient profile that they are currently on anticonvulsant therapy, which aligns with the criterion allowing concurrent anticonvulsant therapy.
